title: Recipes are host-invoked contracts bounded by their declared variant
statement: Every recipe MUST have one canonical source whose manifest validates and whose SKILL.md front matter matches it, its host projections MUST be byte copies of that source, an installation MUST refuse as a whole before its first write when a preflight over every target finds a symlink on any installation path or any drifted target, MUST hold the exclusive repository recipe-install lock (created without replacing an existing lock, removed only by its owner, and refused rather than taken over when stale) from its write-time recheck through every publication and any rollback, MUST recheck every target and its ancestors at write time without following links and refuse when one has become a symlink or differs from its preflight observation, MUST refuse with RECIPE_INSTALL_ESCAPE_DETECTED, naming the residue path and attempting no deletion of it, when a file it published does not resolve, with its parent, inside the repository as the identity its publication returned, and MUST install as one unit that publishes each new file without replacing an existing entry and, on any refusal or failure, removes through that identity-bound removal every file it published (by the identity its publication returned) and every directory it created (by the identity pinned at its creation) that is still that identity and holds no other entry, leaving any other entry found at those paths in place, and reporting as residue any removal the authority broker refuses because it would resolve outside the repository and any directory it created but could not pin, so the prior set of targets remains, and every typed operation MUST run only as part of a manifest-declared variant of a known recipe, with an effect no wider than the variant, explicit repository-relative write paths inside the variant write scope for any non-read operation, and an existing materialized file with different bytes reported as drift rather than overwritten.
rationale: ADR-GOV-0020 keeps one canonical recipe source with generated projections, and the recipe contract keeps deterministic work in typed operations whose effects and write scopes the declared variant bounds; a recipe that widens its scope would act outside any authorized boundary. The symlink and drift refusal runs twice: a preflight over every target, and a write-time recheck by lstat and no-follow reads against the preflight digests, so a target changed or a link inserted after preflight refuses; the ADR-AUT-0005 no-replace publication, which returns the identity of the file it created, a no-follow descriptor that pins each published inode until the installation ends so the identity cannot be reused, and an in-process rollback journal keep a failed installation from leaving a partial set (issue #313). Threat model: the lock excludes concurrent DEVAI installers, and the post-publication realpath and identity check detects an escape after the fact. Node offers no openat, so the checks are path based: a hostile local process that swaps an ancestor for a link between the recheck and the link(2) can make one write land outside the repository before it is detected, reported as residue and refused; preventing that window is outside this statement. Issue #317 closed the cleanup races of that family without widening authority. The broker never authorizes a removal that resolves outside the repository, so an escaped publication is detected and reported, never deleted: an inode identity does not name a directory entry, and a hard link to the published file outside the repository plus an ancestor swap could otherwise make the cleanup delete an entry the publication never created. An identity-bound removal lstat-checks the entry first and leaves any other entry untouched; a matching entry is renamed to a fresh private quarantine name and checked again before it is unlinked or removed by a non-recursive rmdir. A regular file swapped in before the rename is put back by a no-replace hard link; a directory or link swapped in stays in quarantine and the removal refuses with AUTHORITY_REMOVE_RESTORE_INCOMPLETE naming the quarantine path. The broker pins the requested parent with a no-follow directory descriptor at effect time and requires its realpath to be the parent of the authorized canonical target, and its identity the pinned one, immediately before the effect and after it on success or failure, refusing with AUTHORITY_REMOVE_PARENT_ESCAPED (a missing parent too). Residual limits: the escaped file of a detected escape remains outside the repository until a person removes it; a process that finds the random quarantine name and replaces that entry between the rename and the second identity check can still have its entry checked (it is removed only if it carries the identity); a directory or link swapped in between the first check and the rename is left at its quarantine name rather than at its path; Node has no directory-relative rename, so an ancestor swapped and swapped back between the two parent checks is not seen; and a directory another process creates or swaps in at a path between the installer's absence check and the pin after its mkdir is taken for the installer's own, because the broker reports a mkdir of an existing directory as success. A process crash mid-installation is also outside it: it can leave a subset of the new files and the lock, which then refuses as stale until a human removes it, after which a re-run completes the set because files holding the generated bytes are left unchanged.

strategy.rationale: A deterministic test corpus under tests/ and packages/*/tests observes this obligation; trace links the tests.
